rounds.text: Hariyana Ship Breakers Ltd offers a compelling deep-value opportunity, trading at a remarkably low price-to-earnings ratio of 3.4x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.36x against a book value of ₹ 245 [E2]. The business is nearly debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x [E34, E47], and its fundamentals show an explosive recent inflection with trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth surging by 69% [E16] alongside a 316% jump in compounded profit growth [E19]. Furthermore, operational cash generation is robust, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of 8.15x where profits are fully backed by cash [E31], yielding ₹ 3.18 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹ 3.40 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E32, E33]. Promoters continue to demonstrate unwavering confidence by holding a steady 74.95% stake [E38]. Conceded: the company carries contingent liabilities of ₹ 141 Cr [E52], and its discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value below the current market price [E40].

Despite low headline multiples, Hariyana Ship Breakers Ltd carries severe fundamental and valuation risks supported by a rules-based screen score of just 35 out of 100 pointing to a SELL recommendation with medium confidence [E53]. Long-term top-line erosion is severe, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of -53% over 5 years and -60% over 3 years [E14, E15], accompanied by a multi-year trend of dismal profitability where the median return on equity is a meager 2% to 3% across trailing periods [E24, E25, E26]. Operational deterioration is further underlined by an alarming operating margin of -37% in the TTM period, which has plummeted 35 percentage points from three years earlier [E28], alongside a deeply concerning current ratio of 0.19x showing that current liabilities heavily exceed current assets [E35]. Furthermore, massive contingent liabilities of Rs. 141 Cr loom over the balance sheet [E52], and a discounted cash flow model indicates that the intrinsic value sits at Rs. 49 per share against a market price of Rs. 87.5, creating a negative margin of safety of -80.0% [E40, E41]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x and positive trailing cash flows with a strong cash conversion of 8.15x [E31, E34].

Conceded: long-term compounded sales growth over 5 and 3 years sits at -53% and -60% [E14, E15], median 3-year return on equity is low at 2% [E26], operating margins dropped to -37% in the TTM [E28], current liabilities exceed current assets with a current ratio of 0.19x [E35], and contingent liabilities reach Rs. 141 Cr [E52]. However, the bear's discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs. 49 is contradicted by the fact that the stock trades at a deep discount to its asset backing with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.36x against a book value of ₹ 245 [E2]. Furthermore, the bear ignores the dramatic positive inflection in recent fundamentals, specifically trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth surging by 69% [E16], compounded profit growth rocketing by 316% [E19], and an exceptionally robust cash conversion of 8.15x where profits are fully backed by actual operating cash flow [E31]. The balance sheet risks are heavily mitigated by a very conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x alongside positive free cash flow of Rs. 3.40 Cr [E33, E34], while promoter commitment remains rock-solid at 74.95% [E38].

Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is 0.36x against a book value of ₹ 245 [E2], trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth reached 69% [E16], profit growth surged by 316% [E19], and debt-to-equity is 0.04x [E34]. However, asset backing is heavily obscured by massive contingent liabilities of Rs. 141 Cr [E52], which threaten that very book value. The cited short-term growth spikes arrive on the back of a catastrophic multi-year contraction featuring a 5-year sales decline of -53% [E14] and an operating margin that plummeted to -37% in the TTM [E28]. Furthermore, despite positive free cash flow of Rs. 3.40 Cr in March 2026 [E33], the balance sheet faces severe structural strain with a current ratio of just 0.19x, indicating current liabilities drastically exceed current assets [E35]. Finally, promoter holding stability at 74.95% [E38] does nothing to offset a rules-based screen score of 35 out of 100 signaling a SELL with medium confidence [E53].
